faqs.question: How do on-grid rooftop solar systems work?
faqs.answer: Solar photovoltaic (PV) panels absorb sunlight and convert it into direct current (DC) electricity. An on-grid string inverter converts this DC power into standard alternating current (AC) electricity to power your lights, appliances, and machinery. Any excess energy produced during the day is exported to the public grid via a bidirectional net-meter, earning energy credits that reduce your monthly power bill.

faqs.question: How much can I reduce my electricity bill with solar?
faqs.answer: A correctly sized grid-tied solar system typically reduces monthly electricity bills by 70% to 90%. In Eastern India, a 3 kW residential rooftop solar plant generates roughly 360 units (kWh) per month, delivering annual savings of ₹25,000 to ₹30,000 with a full investment payback period of approximately 3 years.

faqs.question: What is the lifespan of solar panels and inverters?
faqs.answer: Tier-1 monocrystalline solar panels have an operational lifespan of 25 to 30 years and come with a 25-year linear performance warranty guaranteeing >= 80% output efficiency at Year 25. High-quality grid-tie string inverters typically have a lifespan of 10 to 15 years and carry 5 to 10-year manufacturer replacement warranties.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy amount under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana?
faqs.answer: Under the Central Government's PM Surya Ghar scheme, residential homeowners receive a fixed financial subsidy of ₹30,000 for a 1 kW system, ₹60,000 for a 2 kW system, and ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW or higher capacity. The subsidy amount is credited directly into the homeowner's bank account following technical inspection and net-meter commissioning.

faqs.question: What documents are required to apply for the solar subsidy?
faqs.answer: You only need four simple documents: (1) Latest electricity bill from your DISCOM (e.g. JBVNL/TSUISL), (2) Aadhaar card of the electricity connection holder, (3) Bank account passbook or cancelled cheque for direct subsidy credit, and (4) Clear rooftop photographs. JDC Solar handles 100% of the National Portal registration and submission on your behalf.

faqs.question: How long does it take to receive the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in my bank account?
faqs.answer: Once the physical installation is complete and the DISCOM installs the bidirectional net-meter, a joint commissioning certificate is uploaded to the National Solar Portal. Subsidies are typically disbursed directly into your bank account via DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) within 30 to 45 days of commissioning.

faqs.question: How much rooftop area is required for a solar installation?
faqs.answer: As a standard engineering benchmark, each 1 kWp of solar panel capacity requires approximately 100 square feet (9.3 square meters) of shadow-free rooftop space. For example, a 3 kW home system requires about 300 sq.ft, while a 250 kW industrial rooftop installation requires about 25,000 sq.ft.

faqs.question: Will solar panel installation damage my roof?
faqs.answer: No. JDC Solar uses non-penetrative anchoring techniques or specialized chemical waterproofing sealant on flat concrete RCC roofs. For industrial metal shed roofs, specialized aluminum rail clamps are used that attach securely to the roof purlins without puncturing or causing water leakage.

faqs.question: What happens on cloudy, rainy, or hazy days?
faqs.answer: Solar panels continue to generate electricity even under diffuse light on overcast and rainy days, producing roughly 25% to 40% of their peak capacity. Because your system is connected to the grid via net-metering, any shortfall in solar power is automatically drawn seamlessly from the utility grid with zero power interruption.
